correctness.rationale: Pollak rotation on N=n+1 circular sites bijects shift-orbit representatives to uniform classical parking functions and preserves lucky indicators and preference-count profiles. Conditioning on preceding preferences, exactly N−i+1 free labels are absent from all earlier preference draws. An independent insertion of draw i changes frequency-r count by binomial difference h_m(r)=b_m(r−1)−b_m(r); conditional covariance gives (N−i+1)/N [h_{n−i}(r)−h_{n−1}(r)]. The first lucky indicator has zero covariance. Binomial second differences show h_m(1) strictly decreases; for r>=3 it increases over a nontrivial range; and h_m(2) increases then decreases, giving a unique positive-to-negative arrival change exactly for n>=5. Poisson limit yields the unique critical lambda in (0,2−sqrt(2)), alpha*=1−lambda≈0.714556. Independently enumerated every classical parking function for n=2,...,6 with exact rational covariance, checking the full formula. Exact Fraction sign computations checked n=2,3,4,5,6,7,10,25,50,100,200 including at most one zero; finite checks do not prove all n.

originality.rationale: Best-of-knowledge: the circular parking law, lucky-count generating functions, and preference species occupancy distribution are prior work. The materially inspected source papers treat their marginal distributions and prescribed lucky subsets, not the mixed arrival-specific covariance of one lucky indicator with each multiplicity class. The conditional insertion formula and doubleton sign reversal are substantive additions and not entailed merely by multiplying marginal generating functions.
residual_risks: Classical linear-probing/hashing literature could contain a reformulation of the same mixed covariance not indexed as parking-function species.
